issue: Expects 'two DNA ladders' as the diagnostic-digest result
why_wrong: A ladder is the molecular-weight standard, not a result. The expected outcome is two insert-derived bands of predicted size per construct, compared against one ladder lane.
reference: Standard practice; band sizes are computable from the plasmid maps (this report, Table 2)
correction: Restate as: two bands at predicted sizes, sized against a single ladder lane. Predicted sizes given in this report.

issue: Cell strain written as 'NHB10 E. coli'
why_wrong: NEB's chemically competent strain used with 10-beta/Stable Outgrowth Medium is NEB 10-beta; 'NHB10' does not correspond to a catalogue strain. The protocol quoted in [9]-[24] is NEB's 10-beta protocol.
reference: NEB 10-beta competent E. coli (C3019); protocol text in [14],[17] names '10-beta/Stable Outgrowth Medium'
correction: Correct to 'NEB 10-beta'. Note the quoted protocol is NEB's own, so the strain name should match it.

why_wrong: The standard treatment is heat-INACTIVATION (56 C, 30 min) to destroy complement. 'Heat-activated' inverts the meaning.

issue: Opti-MEM used only for the DNA+lipid complexes
why_wrong: That is correct for complex formation, but [27] then switches the CULTURE medium to Opti-MEM, which is a reduced-serum medium. Prolonged culture in Opti-MEM without serum slows growth and confounds the cell-count time course that [31] depends on.
reference: Thermo Fisher Lipofectamine 3000 protocol (complexes in Opti-MEM); Opti-MEM product documentation
correction: Keep Opti-MEM for complexes. For the 24-72 h collection, either keep serum-free deliberately (and say so, because it aids supernatant analysis) or keep DMEM+FBS - but do not switch mid-series.

issue: First fluorescence read at 24 h to choose the plasmid
why_wrong: Thermo's own Lipofectamine 3000 comparison data analyse GFP at 48 h post-transfection. A 24 h read is on the rising phase, and IRES vs P2A constructs differ in kinetics, so ranking them at 24 h can invert the ordering seen at 48 h.
reference: Thermo Fisher Lipofectamine 3000 product data (GFP analysed 48 h post-transfection)
correction: Read at 24, 48 and 72 h - they already collect at those points - and rank on the 48 h value.

issue: 'cell count identifies the timepoint with the highest amount of proenkephalin'
why_wrong: Cell number and proenkephalin yield are different quantities. Cell count measures proliferation and lipoplex toxicity; it says nothing about per-cell PENK production. The two can move in opposite directions, because transfection reduces viability while expression rises.
reference: Internal logic; Lipofectamine cytotoxicity documented in Thermo product FAQ
correction: Normalise: report PENK per viable cell (or per mg total protein). Use the cell count as the denominator and a toxicity control, not as the yield read-out.

issue: Isolate PENK by size exclusion alone
why_wrong: Proenkephalin is ~31 kDa and will co-elute with abundant serum and medium proteins of similar size. SEC alone is a fractionation step, not a purification, and there is no affinity handle on these constructs.
reference: General chromatography; construct maps show no epitope tag (this report, Table 2)
correction: Either add a C-terminal tag to the next-generation construct, or follow SEC with an anti-PENK immunoprecipitation / Western step. Note the tag must NOT sit at the C-terminus of cassette 7.

issue: PC1/3 as the primary in vitro convertase, with PC2/7B2/CPE only 'if there is time'
why_wrong: PC2 - not PC1/3 - is responsible for essentially all small-opioid-peptide generation from proenkephalin. Johanning et al. report that generation of small opioid peptides from intermediates is mediated almost entirely by PC2 rather than PC1, and that PC2-knockout brains are depleted of mature enkephalins by more than three quarters. With PC1/3 alone the expected product is intermediates, not enkephalins.
reference: Johanning et al. 1998, J Biol Chem 273:22672-80, doi:10.1074/jbc.273.35.22672
correction: Invert the priority: PC2 + 7B2 is the essential arm, PC1/3 the secondary one. 7B2 is not optional - it is an obligate chaperone for PC2 activity (UniProt P16519/P05408).

issue: No CPE in the primary reaction
why_wrong: Convertase cleavage leaves C-terminal basic residues (K/R). Without carboxypeptidase E the products are Met-enk-Arg / Met-enk-Lys extended forms, not Met-enkephalin itself - so an MS or antibody assay targeting Met-enkephalin can read negative even when cleavage worked.
reference: UniProt P16870 (CPE) function; standard proenkephalin processing pathway
correction: Include CPE in the primary reaction, or explicitly target the +K/+R extended masses in the read-out.

why_wrong: Chromatography gives retention time, which does not identify a peptide. Two different products can co-elute, and the informative comparison here is a specific mass.
reference: This project's own in vitro protocol already computes exact target masses (07_invitro_penk)
correction: Use LC-MS and target the computed masses - Met-enkephalin [M+H]+ 574.2330 is already tabulated in invitro_ms_targets.csv from the earlier work.

issue: 'regardless of the result, we can say from the literature that IRES gives different expression levels'
why_wrong: This states the conclusion independently of the data, which inverts the engineering cycle. The literature prediction is the hypothesis to be tested, not a substitute for the measurement.
reference: Mizuguchi et al. 2000, Mol Ther 1:376-82, doi:10.1006/mthe.2000.0050 (IRES second-gene expression 6-100%, mostly 20-50%, of cap-dependent first-gene expression)
correction: Rewrite as a falsifiable prediction with a number: expect IRES-downstream expression at roughly 20-50% of the cap-dependent gene, and report the measured ratio whatever it is.

issue: Assumes P2A constructs will give 'greater quantity of PENK'
why_wrong: Plausible on expression grounds, but both P2A constructs in this set carry defects that make the comparison non-equivalent: in mEGFP-P2A-PENK the PENK initiator Met is replaced by P2A's proline, and in PENK-P2A-mEGFP an 18-residue P2A remnant stays fused to cassette 7.
reference: Yan et al. 2010, Anal Biochem 399:144-6, doi:10.1016/j.ab.2009.11.032; Liu et al. 2017, Sci Rep 7:2193, doi:10.1038/s41598-017-02460-2; construct analysis in this report
correction: Compare total PENK by Western, but do not treat higher PENK as better unless the product is also correctly processed - measure peptide output, not precursor abundance.

why_wrong: Cycle 1 ([37]-[38]) already compares the constructs' expression; Cycle 2 compares 'which of the 2 constructs expresses more' by fluorescence microscopy. Same question, different instrument.
correction: Merge, or make Cycle 2 answer a different question - e.g. subcellular localisation, which microscopy can do and a plate reader cannot, and which is the actual test of secretion.

issue: siRNA against neprilysin in HEK293T, with a neprilysin-cDNA plasmid as the counterpart
why_wrong: HEK293 does not express neprilysin (MME 0.7 nTPM) or aminopeptidase N (ANPEP 0.1 nTPM). There is no endogenous target to knock down, so a knockdown experiment in this line has no measurable baseline. Their own workaround - co-transfecting MME cDNA - is the right instinct, but it must then be stated as an artificial reconstitution, not as knockdown of an endogenous enzyme.
reference: Human Protein Atlas cell-line RNA (HEK293): MME 0.7, ANPEP 0.1 nTPM
correction: Frame it explicitly as reconstitution: co-transfect MME cDNA to CREATE the degradation activity, then show siRNA removes it. Also note enkephalin is degraded by ANPEP as well as MME, so silencing MME alone is not sufficient in a tissue that has both.

issue: siRNA timepoints at '1 h, 2 h, later'
why_wrong: RNAi acts by degrading mRNA; the protein must then turn over before any effect appears. At 1-2 h post-transfection no knockdown at the protein level is possible, so these timepoints are guaranteed to be negative for reasons unrelated to whether the siRNA works.
reference: Mechanism of RNAi (mRNA cleavage precedes protein depletion); standard siRNA practice is 24-72 h
correction: Move to 24, 48 and 72 h post-transfection and confirm knockdown at the mRNA level (RT-qPCR) as well as by the functional read-out.

issue: Cycle 5 read-out is 'fluorescence/expression' to test enkephalin persistence
why_wrong: mEGFP reports transfection and translation of the reporter; it does not report enkephalin concentration or its half-life. Neprilysin knockdown cannot change mEGFP fluorescence.
reference: Construct architecture - mEGFP is a separate translation product from PENK in all four plasmids (this report, Table 2)
correction: The read-out must be the peptide: LC-MS or ELISA on the supernatant at each timepoint. Use fluorescence only to normalise for transfection efficiency between wells.

issue: Six cycles here vs three in the dry-lab record
why_wrong: The guide's Cycles 1-6 do not map onto the repository's cycles 1-3b, which cover a different question entirely (binding-mode scoring). Two independent numbering schemes are in use for 'the engineering cycles' of one project.
correction: Adopt one scheme. Suggested: keep the guide's wet-lab numbering as the project record and re-label the dry-lab work as computational sub-cycles, so 'Cycle 3' is unambiguous.
